newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government's commission on elected representatives' remuneration has suggested scrapping "economically indefensible" perks for MPs of the old order and recommended an eight percent pay rise for current MPs.

- The rand gained six cents against the dollar and three cents against the pound on Thursday folowing Wednesday's one percentage point rise in the Bank rate, but traders warned that investor sentiment remained negative and the currency might not hold on to its gains for long.
- Former president PW Botha was adament on Thursday that he was "not guilty of any deed" requiring an apology or an application to the truth commission for amnesty.

- Overspending on health, education and welfare continued to haunt provincial treasuries as they prepared for leaner days under a tight, formula-based budgeting process, provincial sources said Thursday.
- An agreement in principle reached in the transport industry on Thursday could end the truckers' strike, which saw roads blocked and a traffic officer assaulted.

- Government had made progress towards the full privatisation of Sun Air and cash-strapped state-owned resort company Aventura, and both should be in private hands by March, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Thursday.

- The rand firmed four cents against the dollar on Thursday, welcoming the Reserve Bank's one percentage point increase in the Bank rate and announcements by the commercial banks that they would follow suit.

- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is ready to help South Africa with a standby facility to support its reserves but the government does not want to use the loan, a senior IMF official said on Wednesday.

- The two-day old national transport strike could be called off today (Friday) after the Road Freight Association and a seven-union strike committee agreed on wages and working conditions during marathon mediation talks.
- Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd may announce the identity of the party that will acquire a controlling stake in JCI Ltd, its unbundled mining house, next week, according to unconfirmed reports.

- Former state president P W Botha on Thursday indicated a willingness to assist the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in its continuing probe into human rights abuses, but said he had nothing to apologise for and would not seek amnesty.
- Three major commercial banks have already announced increases in their home loan and prime overdraft rates, following the one percentage point hike announced by the Reserve Bank on Wednesday.
